description_full: NH Foods Ltd. engages in manufacturing and selling ham, sausage, processed food, meat, and dairy product in Japan and internationally. The company offers ham and sausages under the SCHAU ESSEN brand; Chinese food meal kits under the Chuka Meisai brand; chilled pizza under the Ishigama Kobo brand; and other meat product under the Hokkaido Carl Ramon and Kamakura Ham Tomioka brands. It also provides dairy products, such as cheese and yogurt products. In addition it involved in the production and raising, slaughtering, processing, distribution, and sale of fresh meat products, as well as engages in the operation of a football club, baseball club, and ballpark. The company was formerly known as Nippon Meat Packers Inc. and changed its name to NH Foods Ltd. in June 2014. NH Foods Ltd. was founded in 1942 and is headquartered in Osaka, Japan.

financial_summary: NH FOODS LTD is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.5B market cap on $9.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 16% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $302M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 7.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
